subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw own pace-aware Anthropic/autonomous-agent throttling in core, and if so should the first scope be read-only pace visibility or enforcement?
rationale: The request adds new provider-specific semantics, config defaults, persisted runtime state, and autonomous agent policy that repository guidance treats as compatibility-sensitive product surface.

options.title: Fold Into Resource Governance
options.body: Use this issue as part of a broader rate-limit, provider-pool, and budget design before introducing a standalone agents.defaults.pace surface.

options.title: Ship Read-Only Pace First
options.body: Add pace projection to status/session_status without automatic throttling while enforcement semantics remain unsettled.

options.title: Route Out Of Core
options.body: Keep core to generic provider usage seams and ask for a plugin or skill implementation unless missing core APIs are identified.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Resource Governance
recommendation.body: Use this issue as part of a broader rate-limit, provider-pool, and budget design before introducing a standalone agents.defaults.pace surface.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the only identified current-main history candidate across the relevant provider-usage and auth-profile files, though provenance is broad and weak.
